newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees signs of economic growth in Jan-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees signs of economic growth in Jan-Feb.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday there were signs of growth in the Russian economy at the start of the year.
Gross domestic product and industrial output had grown in January and February compared with the same period of 1996, he told the cabinet.
Russia was recording such year-on-year growth at the start of the year for the first time in a decade, he said.
Chernomyrdin said incomes were also growing and the number of people with incomes below the level needed to survive was falling.
President Boris Yeltsin said earlier that GDP would grow at least two percent this year.

GDP fell six percent last year and has been falling every year since Russia became independent with the break-up of the Soviet Union in 1991, and is now only 61 percent of 1991 levels, according to official statistics.
In January GDP was 0.1 percent higher than a year earlier. February data have not yet been released.
